International Copper Study Group  
 
 
 
       ICSG/IAP11/3 
Industry Advisory Panel 
14 April 2011, 3.50pm – 5.30pm 
Lisbon, Portugal 
 
 
 
 
Industry Advisory Panel 
Draft Minutes 
 
1. Opening of the Meeting and Report of the Previous IAP Meeting 
 
The Industry Advisory Panel met on 14 April in Lisbon.  Industry advisers were present 
from a wide range of member countries along with industry association, government and 
secretariat representatives.  The Chairman opened the proceedings by informing the 
participants that the Industry Advisory Panel provides an opportunity for industry advisers 
to meet as a group, raise issues to the attention of government members and provide 
feedback, guidance and advice to the Group on its priorities, programs and activities. 
 
The report of the previous IAP meeting in London was presented to facilitate a discussion 
of outstanding issues (ICSG/IAPLondon10/2). 
 
2. Adoption of the Agenda 
(Document ICSG/IAP 11/1) 
 
The Agenda was adopted as tabled. 
 
3. Industry’s Views on Emerging Issues of Interest 
 
a. Access to Raw Materials 
 
Ms Heli Kask of the European Commission spoke to the Panel on the recently-adopted EU 
strategy on raw materials and commodities.  In 2008 the European Commission had adopted a 
Raw Materials Initiative (RMI) which was based on three pillars: ensure access to raw 
materials from global markets; foster sustainable supply within the EU; and boost resource 
efficiency and recycling. As part of this initiative, 14 critical raw materials were identified. 
The latest EU Communication sets out a way forward for the RMI and responds to 
developments in global community markets.  The Commission will monitor issues related to 
critical materials and update the list every three years.  
 
Raw Materials Diplomacy is a tool that the Commission will use to ensure access to global 
markets and this encompasses greater cooperation with Africa, expanded use of financial 
incentives, trade dialogue and other actions. In order to foster supply within the EU, the 
Commission will promote best practices in national minerals policy, land use planning and 
minerals exploration and authorization systems. The Commission will encourage urban 
mining, review the thematic strategy on waste prevention and recycling, develop ecodesign 
instruments and strengthen waste shipment regulations, with a view to boosting efficiency and 
recycling.  
 
Ms Kask then responded to questions, including from IWCC, on the need to ensure that 
regulations do not have unintended consequences for the industry. 
 
 
 
 
2 
 
b. Joint Study Groups’ Seminar “Materials Stewardship for Mining and Metals” 
 
The secretariat provided bullet point outcomes of the Joint Study Groups’ Seminar 
“Materials Stewardship for Mining and Metals” that had been held the previous day to 
facilitate a discussion amongst industry representatives.  Key points to come out of the 
Seminar presentations and subsequent discussion included: 
 
• 
The topic of stewardship is vast and complex encompassing production and 
consumption as well as social, health and safety issues 
• 
A life-cycle approach is central to stewardship.  This includes supply chain 
management and the concept of chain of custody. 
• 
Complexity and confusion are part of stewardship – it was suggested that REACH 
is “the most complex legislation in the EU’s history”  
• 
Stewardship sometimes has unanticipated benefits e.g. the process to implement  
REACH improved communication and helped producers build better relationships 
• 
A wide range of programs and initiatives, both government and private,  focus on 
stewardship, some on specific commodities (Green Lead, Responsible Aluminium), 
others on energy efficiency or emissions 
• 
Improved communication amongst all stakeholders is needed and is possible. The 
example of a recent International Copper Association information session at the 
European Parliament was cited. 
 
In subsequent discussion it was agreed that Stewardship would be an increasingly 
important issue for the industry. 
 
c. Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) 
 
The secretariat provided industry advisors with a brief summary of the presentations 
made earlier in the day at the Environmental & Economic Committee on the 
development of ETFs and the potential impact of financial sector involvement in the 
copper market.  
 
4. Guidance from industry advisors on what work the Study Group should be 
undertaking 
 
The secretariat prepared and presented a document (ICSG/IAP11/2) based on the results of 
the survey undertaken at the September 2010 Industry Advisory Panel meeting in 
Antofagasta, Chile on “Issues for Possible Future Study Group Attention”. Industry 
advisors had discussed these survey results at the IAP meeting held in London on 14 
October 2010 and had asked the secretariat to produce a document that indicated for each 
issue or topic where further work is needed, who is already active or doing work on the 
topic, how ICSG can bring additional value, and how feasible it is for ICSG to do the work 
with limited resources. 
 
A revised version of the table “Issues for Possible Future Study Group Attention”, updated 
to take into account comments made at the meeting, is provided as an attachment to this 
report.

3 
 
Industry representatives reiterated the importance of the Study Group’s work on regulations 
affecting copper, improving semis capacity and production data, and analysing the global 
copper scrap market.   
 
On end use the Secretary-General noted that ICA and IWCC were active in this field, and 
suggested that ICSG might get closer to the work by, for example, playing a dissemination 
role utilising the ICSG Yearbook and other means. 
 
On exploration and investment the Australian representative suggested that the important 
work done by Geoscience Australia and ABARES should be acknowledged, and the 
possibility of the Study Group disseminating the U. S. Geological Survey work on copper 
resources and reserves was also mentioned. 
 
A representative of German industry proposed that any work on technologies affecting 
copper production could also look at what technologies exist to recover metals and at what 
prices they might be viable, and what prices are needed to create investment in various 
technologies for mining, processing and recycling. 
 
It was suggested that any work the Study Group might undertake or commission on the 
impact of financial institutions on the copper market or on price volatility be combined.  
Representatives of Italy, Belgium and France indicated that priority should be given to this 
topic. France also expressed interest in possible work on copper co-products/by-products. 
 
It was also proposed that the Group should continue to have regular presentations on the 
work that is being undertaken on price substitution by, for example, ICA and IWCC. It was 
suggested also that the Study Group could undertake every few years a project on one 
specific end use application. 
 
In the discussion industry advisors were also invited to comment on the Study Group’s 
current Work Program and to suggest possible topics for work in the future (EEC Work 
Program Document ICSG/EEC30/6 & Statistical Committee Work Program Document 
ICSG/STAT37/5). 
 
In concluding the discussions the Chairman noted that the comments from industry 
representatives would provide important guidance to the Study Group in formulating its 
future work programs. 
 
5. Election of the IAP Chairman 
 
Mr Mark Loveitt (IWCC) was re-elected as Chairman of the Industry Advisory Panel. 
 
6. Arrangements for the Chairman's Report 
 
The Chairman advised Panel members that a report would be prepared and distributed 
following the meeting.
